transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. Before we dive in, could you tell me what brings you here today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I explain this right... please just let me know if I'm rambling or if you need me to be more specific. 

But I came in because, well, my schedule just got a little... overwhelming, I guess? I went from barely being able to unpack and settle into my new apartment to suddenly just... doing everything all at once. I started saying yes to all these mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes for my design work, and I even decided to completely redesign my whole portfolio out of nowhere. It was like I suddenly had to fix my entire life in one massive sprint. 

Which, I mean, being driven and productive is supposed to be a good thing, right? I know it sounds like I'm just complaining about being a hard worker. But it just felt a bit much, and I got a little worried about myself. Does that... does that sound like the kind of thing you can help with?
During this period of increased activity, have you noticed a change in how much sleep you need—for example, feeling rested after just a few hours, or not needing to sleep much at all?

Well, um... yes, actually. But I don't want it to sound like I was being reckless with my health or anything! I know how important sleep is. It's just... for several nights in a row, I think I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours? 

But the weird thing is, I didn't feel tired. I'd wake up and honestly feel totally fine, like I had a full night's rest. So I just figured, you know, why not use the extra time to get ahead on all those projects? I hope that doesn't sound too irresponsible... I just really wanted to make the most of feeling so energized. Is that... is that normal when you're just really focused on work?
How long has this period of feeling unusually energetic and needing less sleep lasted so far—days, or longer?

Um, well... I guess the whole thing has been going on for a little while now. Not just the energy, but sort of... everything? This whole intense up-and-down pattern has been happening since I moved into my new apartment, which was about a month ago. 

I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I mean, moving is stressful for everyone, right? It's totally normal to be a little unsettled. But yeah, it's been about a month of this... back and forth. Does that... does that timeframe make sense to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Aside from this energetic period, have you ever had separate stretches of time—lasting a couple of weeks or more—where you felt persistently down, low on energy, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Um... well, yes, I suppose so. I really don't want to sound like I'm just wallowing or complaining, though. I know everyone gets in a slump sometimes. But... if I'm being completely honest, I have had some heavier stretches where it was just really hard to get going. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, but... they started showing up around 11 months ago, after a separation. I hope it's okay to bring that up—I don't want to overshare or make excuses! But yeah, since the separation about 11 months ago, I've had these longer periods of feeling really down and just kind of empty. And then the latest move just sort of made everything sharper, I guess? 

I just assumed I wasn't handling all these life transitions very gracefully. I mean, it's normal to struggle a bit after a breakup, right? Does that... does that answer your question? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

During those down periods after your separation, did you notice things like a big change in your appetite or weight, trouble concentrating, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or any thoughts of not wanting to be alive—and did these problems make it hard to function at work or with people?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't sound like I'm just letting myself go or not taking care of myself properly. I know I should be eating better. But during those lower times, especially recently... it's just that most days, food feels like another chore on my to-do list? 

I don't want to make a big deal out of it, but I usually just end up picking at some crackers, or I'll order something and then barely touch it. I guess my appetite just kind of... disappears. And, um, I have noticed my jeans are hanging a bit looser than they did when I moved in. 

I'm still trying my best, though! I know I need to force myself to eat. I just... I hope you don't think I'm being negligent with my health. Is it... is it common to just lose interest in eating when you're feeling down like that? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you a very good answer...

During that period of high energy and reduced sleep, did it cause any serious problems—like trouble at work, conflicts with people, or situations where others felt you needed to be stopped or helped—or were you still able to manage your daily responsibilities without major disruption?

Um... well, I really try my best to keep on top of everything, I promise. I don't want to make it sound like my life is completely falling apart, because I'm usually very organized and responsible! But... I guess during that really energetic time, I did drop the ball a little bit. 

I feel awful even admitting this, and I really hope you don't judge me too harshly, but... I actually missed a design review at work. I just got so caught up in a million other ideas and it completely slipped my mind. I felt terrible about it. And, um, because of things like that... I've sort of been avoiding my friends and family recently. Not because I don't care about them! I just... I feel so embarrassed about how scattered and unreliable I've seemed lately. I don't want them to worry, or to think I'm flaky. 

I just want everyone to see the best version of me, you know? Is that... is it understandable to want to hide away a little when you feel like you're letting people down? I really am trying to get back on track and fix it, I promise.
Thinking specifically about that stretch of high energy and reduced need for sleep—about how many days in a row did that particular period last?

Um... well, it's a little hard to pin down the exact number of days, I suppose. I really hope I'm remembering this right—I don't want to give you the wrong information! But... I guess this whole intense up-and-down pattern, including that really energetic stretch, has been going on since I moved into my new apartment. 

That was about a month ago. I just... I figured it was all the stress of unpacking and settling in, you know? Moving is always so chaotic, so I thought maybe I was just running on adrenaline for a while. I really didn't think it was anything too out of the ordinary, and I certainly didn't mean to let it get out of hand. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of timeline you were looking for...
During that energetic stretch, did it last at least a full week without a break, or was it shorter than that?

Um... gosh, I really wish I had kept a better journal or something so I could give you a perfectly accurate answer. I'm sorry if I'm being vague! But... no, I don't think it was a full week straight. 

If I'm being completely honest—and I really hope this doesn't make me sound too erratic—it was probably more like... four or five days? Maybe? It definitely wasn't a whole week without a break. I just... I tried really hard to reel it in and get back to a normal schedule as quickly as I could. I know how important sleep is! I didn't want to just let myself spiral, you know? 

So, yeah, it was shorter than a week. Is... is four or five days still helpful for you to know? I hope I'm not making things too complicated...

I'm so sorry, I think I might have missed what you just asked. Could you possibly repeat it for me? I just want to be absolutely sure I'm giving you the right information and not wasting your time. I really hope I'm doing okay with all these questions...

During those four or five days of high energy, did you also notice your mood itself feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable—different from your normal mood—or was it mainly just the energy and activity level that changed?

Um... well, yes, I suppose my mood was a little different, too. I really hope this doesn't sound terrible, but... earlier this month, during that stretch, I just felt so upbeat. Almost electric, you know? Like everything was just clicking perfectly and I was on top of the world. 

But then... gosh, I feel awful admitting this... I would suddenly just snap. Like, I yelled at a contractor who was helping with the apartment, and I even snapped at my sister over these tiny, insignificant delays. It felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting things done, which I know sounds so unreasonable now! I'm usually very patient, I promise. I always try to be accommodating. 

So, I guess it was a mix of feeling really, really good, and then just getting frustrated so easily. I really hope that doesn't make me seem like a difficult person. Does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

Additionally, the depressive periods appear to meet full criteria for major depressive episodes (appetite/weight loss, anhedonia, social withdrawal, functional impact), which is inconsistent with cyclothymic disorder (F34.0), ruling that out as well. This pattern of full depressive episodes plus a shorter hypomanic episode best fits Bipolar II Disorder (F31.81), with F31.9 retained as a fallback given some uncertainty in symptom count/duration.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the elevated-energy period involved a clear change in mood (elevated, expansive, or irritable) rather than just increased activity/energy, which is a core criterion for a hypomanic episode
doctor.question: During those four or five days of high energy, did you also notice your mood itself feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable—different from your normal mood—or was it mainly just the energy and activity level that changed?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Earlier this month I felt almost electric and upbeat one minute, then snapped at a contractor or my sister over tiny delays like they were personally trying to block me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if my mood was unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable during the high-energy period, which maps directly to the Elevated_Irritable_Mood symptom.

patient.answer:
Um... well, yes, I suppose my mood was a little different, too. I really hope this doesn't sound terrible, but... earlier this month, during that stretch, I just felt so upbeat. Almost electric, you know? Like everything was just clicking perfectly and I was on top of the world. 

But then... gosh, I feel awful admitting this... I would suddenly just snap. Like, I yelled at a contractor who was helping with the apartment, and I even snapped at my sister over these tiny, insignificant delays. It felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting things done, which I know sounds so unreasonable now! I'm usually very patient, I promise. I always try to be accommodating. 

So, I guess it was a mix of feeling really, really good, and then just getting frustrated so easily. I really hope that doesn't make me seem like a difficult person. Does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

inference.note: The patient now describes a clear hypomanic episode (elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, distractibility, mild functional impairment without psychosis or hospitalization) lasting 4-5 days, plus distinct major depressive episodes with anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, and low energy. This pattern is consistent with Bipolar II disorder, ruling out unspecified bipolar disorder (F31.9) as the clinical picture is now sufficiently characterized.

opening_question.intent: Establish the primary reason for the visit today
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome in. Before we dive in, could you tell me what brings you here today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a distinct 4-5 day period of elevated/euphoric and irritable mood with decreased need for sleep (3-4 hours without fatigue), increased goal-directed activity (taking on multiple projects, redesigning portfolio), and impulsive overcommitment leading to functional consequences (missed work review, interpersonal friction with contractor and sister). This meets criteria for hypomanic episode (≥4 consecutive days, ≥3 associated symptoms, observable change, causing some functional disruption but not requiring hospitalization). Separately, patient endorses a major depressive episode with depressed/empty mood, anhedonia, and appetite/weight loss lasting >2 weeks, onset ~11 months ago after a separation, consistent with a mood disorder involving both hypomanic and depressive episodes. The combination of a major depressive episode plus a hypomanic episode (not full mania) supports Bipolar II Disorder, current episode hypomanic (F31.81).
